html:
Company: Cotton T-shirts producer · Home country: United Kingdom · Size: Small (<50 staff) · HS 610910 (Textiles & apparel) · Trade data 2019-2024

1. Executive Summary

Verdict: ENTER. Attractive market with manageable risks.

Market attractiveness: 6.8/10
Recommended entry mode: Exclusive distributor or agent, with a small local sales office

  • Import market of €6.64 bn in 2024, trend growth +2.2% a year (data confidence: high).
  • Supply is highly concentrated (HHI 2,746); top supplier Bangladesh holds 48.67%.
  • CAGE distance from United Kingdom: low.
  • Applicable import duty: 0% (Preferential rate under EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement, published by WITS for 2021 (rules of origin apply; MFN 12.0% otherwise)); landed cost ≈ +4% over ex-works price before VAT.
  • United Kingdom is supplier #10 with 1.27% of imports, priced premium (3.14x market average per kg).
  • China supplies 6.49% of extra-EU imports.
  • Priority EU markets: Germany, Netherlands, Ireland.

4. PESTEL Analysis

  • Political: Stable democracies with a single trade policy run by the European Commission. EU-China relations follow a 'de-risking' agenda: more trade-defence cases, the Foreign Subsidies Regulation and screening of Chinese investment.
  • Economic: Single market of ~450 million consumers and one of the world's largest import markets; high purchasing power, though growth is modest and varies strongly between member states. Latest: GDP growth 1.5% (2025), inflation 2.5% (World Bank).
  • Social: Diverse languages and consumer cultures across 27 countries; strong demand for sustainability, quality and data privacy; ageing population.
  • Technological: Advanced digital infrastructure and e-commerce; strict standards (CE, EN norms) make quality and certification a competitive factor.
  • Environmental: European Green Deal: CBAM, Ecodesign/ESPR, Battery Regulation, deforestation and packaging rules raise compliance costs but reward low-carbon products.
  • Legal: Harmonised product law across the EU (one CE mark for 27 markets), GDPR for customer data, strong IP protection and contract enforcement.

6. Tariffs, Trade Defence & Regulation

Import duty

  • MFN applied tariff of EU-27: 12%, 2023 (World Bank WITS / UNCTAD TRAINS (MFN applied, simple average)).
  • Likely rate for a company from United Kingdom: 0% (Preferential rate under EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement, published by WITS for 2021 (rules of origin apply; MFN 12.0% otherwise)).

Indicative landed cost (per 100 of ex-works value)

Item Amount Assumption
Goods (ex-works) 100.00
Freight & insurance 3.00 3% for low distance
Import duty 0.00 0% on CIF value
Clearance, broker, port 1.50 1.5%
Import VAT 19.57 19% (Germany), usually recoverable for VAT-registered importers
Landed cost 124.07 104.50 before VAT (+4.5%)

Regulatory checklist

  • Textile Labelling Regulation 1007/2011; REACH restrictions on substances
  • Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) and the coming Digital Product Passport; ban on destroying unsold apparel
  • General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988 (GPSR), applies to consumer products since Dec 2024
  • Union Customs Code: an EU-established importer/representative and EORI number are required
  • Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015: ban on products made with forced labour, applies from Dec 2027

Official texts: Textile Labelling Regulation 1007/2011 · Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation · GPSR, Regulation (EU) 2023/988 · Union Customs Code · Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015

Regulatory notes compiled 2026-11-21 from official sources; not legal advice.

Verify current duties and requirements: - Access2Markets (EU tariffs, rules of origin, requirements) - EU TARIC tariff database - EU trade defence cases

7. Risk Matrix

Exchange rate (ECB reference rates): GBP per EUR: -2.9% over 2023-10–2026-10 (home currency stronger), annualised volatility 3.0%. Risk level: Low.

Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation
Dominant incumbent supplier (Bangladesh, 48.67% share) High High Differentiate on quality, service, sustainability and EU/China-specific certification rather than price.
Brand and message mis-fit with local consumers Medium Medium Local consumer testing, native-language content, local marketplace and social channels.
Currency volatility (GBP/EUR, 3.0% annualised volatility) Low Medium Price in home currency where possible; hedge large contracts with forwards.

8. Recommended Entry Mode

Exclusive distributor or agent, with a small local sales office

  • Balances control and cost for a mid-attractiveness market.
  • A distributor brings market access; a sales office protects the brand and gathers market intelligence.
  • Home-country exports are priced above the market average: position on quality and brand, with selective distribution.
  • Within the EU one CE-compliant product and one importer of record give access to all 27 markets: start with 2-3 priority countries.
  • Inputs: attractiveness 6.8/10, CAGE distance low, institutional quality 6.8/10, company size small (<50 staff).

Sensitivity to the weights

The weights are a judgement call, so the same sub-scores are re-weighted under alternative schemes:

Weighting scheme Score
Base case 6.8
Equal weights 6.8
Size-led (large incumbents) 6.9
Growth-led (start-ups) 6.5

Robust: the score stays between 6.5 and 6.9, and the verdict band does not change.

10. 90-Day Action Plan

  1. Days 1-30, validate: confirm the HS code and duty rate on official tariff tools, size the niche with customer interviews, shortlist 10 potential partners or channels in Germany, Netherlands, Ireland.
  2. Days 1-30, compliance: map required certifications and labelling (see section 6), get quotes from a test lab or regulatory agent, register trademarks in the target market.
  3. Days 31-60, commercial model: build a landed-cost and pricing model (duties, freight, VAT, channel margins, FX), and draft the partner or channel agreement.
  4. Days 31-60, go-to-market: localise product pages, packaging and sales material; pick 1-2 launch channels consistent with the entry mode: exclusive distributor or agent, with a small local sales office.
  5. Days 61-90, pilot: ship a pilot order or open the online store, track sell-through, margin and customer feedback against go/no-go KPIs.
